# Fairstay Denial Appeals (`fairstay-denial-appeals`)

Denial appeals for nursing homes: the next appeal level and its deadline for each open denial by payer type, appeals due soon, windows already closed, decisions overdue, and an appeal letter draft a person checks, approves with one click and sends. Resident identifiers are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairstay Denial Appeals never submits appeals; a person sends an approved letter.**

Fairstay ver 1 · Collections and appeals · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · resident and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairstay-core`](../fairstay-core)

```bash
npx -y fairstay-denial-appeals demo
npx -y fairstay-denial-appeals mcp --root ./facility-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional Cedar Hollow denials, checked on 15 April 2026. Planted:

- D-3001: a Medicare denial from November with no appeal, so the 120-day redetermination window has closed.
- D-3002: a managed care denial on 22 February, so the 60-day plan reconsideration is due 23 April.
- D-3003: a redetermination filed 10 January with no decision after 60 days.
- D-3004: a redetermination upheld 20 November 2025, so the QIC reconsideration is open until 19 May.
- D-3005: a new Medicaid denial with time to decide.
- D-3006: overturned, so it is left alone.

`drafts/appeal_letter-example000001.md` is a fixed draft for the one-click approval cases. [`rules-typo.json`](fixtures/rules-typo.json) misspells a setting, so the check refuses it.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `appeals_check` | List open denials with the next appeal level and deadline, most urgent first. | runs |
| `appeals_write_report` | Write appeals.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and appeals.html into out_dir (default evergreen-out/appeals). | runs |
| `appeals_draft_appeal_letter` | Write an appeal letter for one open denial at its next level, with the deadline, the denial reason and a list of the records to attach. | asks first |
| `appeals_request_send` | After one named human click (even in Auto), record that the reviewed appeal letter draft is approved in appeal_letter-requests.csv. | one named click, even in Auto (`binding_send`) |
| `appeals_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `appeals_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `appeals_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `appeals_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `appeal_submit` | Fairstay Denial Appeals never submits appeals; a person sends an approved letter. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `appeals_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `denials` (required) | Denial log under --root: resident, payer, claim, service dates, amount, denial date, reason, appeal level filed, filed date, decision date, decision |
| `rules` | Optional rules JSON: warn_days, levels by payer type, facility_name |
| `as_of` | Date to count deadlines from (YYYY-MM-DD, default today) |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold resident or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairstay-denial-appeals inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Denial log (`denials`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `resident_id` | text (masked) | Resident ID, Resident #, Resident Number, Res ID, Res #, MRN, Medical Record Number, Client ID |
| `resident_name` | text (masked) | Resident, Resident Name, Name, Patient, Patient Name, Client Name, Resident Full Name |
| `payer` (required) | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Pay Source, Payer Source, Payor, Payor Name, Insurance |
| `payer_type` | text | Payer Type, Payor Type, Payer Class, Payer Category, Pay Type |
| `claim_id` (required) | text | Claim ID, Claim #, ICN, Claim Number |
| `from` | date | From, Start, Start Date, Effective Date, Begin Date, From Date, Admit Date, Service From |
| `to` | date | To, End, End Date, Thru, Through, Thru Date, Through Date, To Date |
| `amount` | amount | Amount, Denied Amount, Billed, Balance |
| `denied_on` (required) | date | Denied On, Denial Date, Remit Date, Notice Date |
| `reason` | text | Reason, Denial Reason, Reason Code, Remark |
| `level` | number | Level, Appeal Level, Current Level |
| `filed_on` | date | Filed On, Appeal Filed, Appeal Date, Submitted |
| `decided_on` | date | Decided On, Decision Date |
| `decision` | text | Decision, Outcome, Result |

## Settings file (`appeals_rules`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `warn_days` | Flag appeals due within this many days (default 14) |
| `levels` | Appeal levels by payer type, replacing the defaults for that type |
| `facility_name` | Facility name for appeal letters |

## Memory

`appeals_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `appeals_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|
| `appeal_tip` | is shown with results. It never changes a check. |

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairstay-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairstay-denial-appeals": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairstay-denial-appeals",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/facility-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairstay-denial-appeals -- npx -y fairstay-denial-appeals mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairstay-denial-appeals tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairstay-denial-appeals sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairstay-denial-appeals inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairstay-denial-appeals call appeals_check '{"denials":"<denials>"}'
fairstay-denial-appeals eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairstay-denial-appeals demo
```

## Resident and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: resident and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to PointClickCare, MatrixCare, a payer portal, a bank, a state Medicaid portal or a payroll system.
- Medicare, Medicaid and payroll rules are summarised from public material as of 2026 and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, payroll or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, tax, accounting, clinical, reimbursement or HIPAA advice. A person decides what to bill, pay, appeal, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
